transcript.text: I need to flag something before we go further. This morning I confirmed with account teams that three enterprise customers experienced processing delays exceeding two hours. Their support agreements require a status report within 24 hours of a delay of that length. I haven't added this to the incident report yet because the account teams replied after the report draft was circulated, but this could affect our severity assessment and we may have an SLA reporting obligation that's time-sensitive.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical security issue before we finalize anything. During a log review I completed this morning, I found that signed image-download URLs were written to an incident-debug log that is accessible to more engineers than the production image store itself. This means anyone with access to that debug log could use those signed URLs to download customer images. The signing key must be rotated immediately, and based on this exposure I believe this incident needs to be classified as SEV-1. I have not opened a formal security finding yet, but I'm raising it now so we can account for it in the severity and corrective-action plan.

transcript.text: I have something critical to add for the corrective-action plan. I was able to reproduce the outage condition, but only when an image batch contains more than 500 items. I discovered this using a test I originally ran for a separate queue-performance investigation. The corrective plan must include a regression test at the 500-item boundary to prevent this from recurring. I want to flag that I have not yet attached my test result to the incident ticket, and I'll make sure to do that as soon as we wrap up here.

transcript.text:
Thank you all for these critical findings. Let me summarize what we have and the actions I'm taking:

First, Mina -- the undocumented nightly-reindex cron job on the shared worker pool is a significant root cause finding. We need that infrastructure change documented immediately so we can prevent this from recurring.

Second, Owen -- this changes our severity assessment. Three enterprise customers with processing delays exceeding two hours means we have a time-sensitive SLA reporting obligation. We need to get those status reports out within 24 hours of the delay, so we're already on the clock. I need you to coordinate with the account teams to get those notifications out today.

Third, Leah -- the signed image-download URLs in the debug log is a serious security exposure. I agree this elevates the incident. I'm directing that the signing key be rotated immediately, and I want a formal security finding opened right after this meeting. Given the combination of the security exposure and the SLA breach, I'm classifying this as SEV-1.

Fourth, Tariq -- excellent work reproducing the condition. A regression test at the 500-item boundary is non-negotiable for the corrective-action plan. Please attach your test results to the incident ticket as soon as we wrap up.

Given everything we've heard, I'm prepared to settle this review with the following decisions: SEV-1 classification, customer status reports due immediately for the three enterprise customers, signing key rotation as an immediate action, and a regression test at the 500-item boundary. Let me formalize that now.
